documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Syllabus Guidance
documents.stance_why: The page requires every instructor to include a gen-AI policy and says "Instructors have the academic freedom to decide what degree of generative AI use" applies, so it sets no university-wide stance and gives sample language only.
documents.summary: Academic Affairs requires a generative AI statement in every syllabus and leaves the degree of use to instructors and assignments. A sample statement asks students to cite and verify AI output and to ask when unsure.

units.why: "All Marshall instructors are required to have a generative AI policy in their syllabi" is a university mandate binding instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, which is exactly P09 and is communicated before the course runs.
units.anchor: All Marshall instructors are required to have a generative AI policy in their syllabi.

units.why: The passage says the syllabus policy "should promote ethical decision making" and "mirrors industry/discipline norms, needs, and standards", tying course rules to career preparation. It is a rationale about professional AI use (P44), not a stance rule (P02), since it sets no default.
units.anchor: mirrors industry/discipline norms, needs, and standards

units.why: "Instructors have the academic freedom to decide what degree of generative AI use should be integrated" hands the decision to instructors per activity and assignment, so P04 and not a university default.
units.anchor: Instructors have the academic freedom to decide

units.why: The sample syllabus text says students "may not use generative AI in any way that would violate the Student Code of Conduct", classing improper AI use under the existing conduct code. P36 fits better than P19 because it forbids no specific use, only conduct-code violations.
units.anchor: use generative AI in any way that would violate the

units.why: "You may be allowed to use Generative AI in some ways but are prohibited from using it in other ways" in the sample statement makes permission depend on the individual assignment or activity, so P04 rather than P01 or P02.
units.anchor: use Generative AI in some ways but are prohibited from using it in other ways
units.frag_start: You may be allowed to use

units.why: "Some assignments prohibit AI use entirely" states that individual assignments may ban AI outright, a per-assignment rule (P04); it is not a course default so P01 does not fit.
units.anchor: Some assignments prohibit AI use entirely.

units.why: The sample policy says AI use "should be considered just like any other personal communication or secondary source of information", which treats AI like an outside source under existing rules (P45).
units.anchor: just like any other personal communication or secondary source of information
units.frag_start: Generative AI use in this course

units.why: The sample policy says AI output must be "critiqued, cross-referenced with primary sources of information", which is a duty to verify and evaluate AI output (P31).
units.anchor: critiqued, cross-referenced with primary sources of information
units.frag_start: Generative AI use in this course

units.why: The same sentence requires AI use to be "properly cited" and points to the library citation guide; this is an AI citation duty (P24). P25 does not fit because no tool, prompt or date details are specified.
units.anchor: and properly cited.
units.frag_start: Generative AI use in this course

units.why: "If there is any ambiguity about generative AI use in the course, please discuss with the instructor" tells students to ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: If there is any ambiguity about generative AI use in the course

units.why: "The instructor should provide specific guidance on if and how AI usage is prohibited or allowed" for each assignment asks instructors to state expectations at assignment level (P09, which also covers assignment instructions).
units.anchor: The instructor should provide specific guidance on if and how AI usage

units.why: "Departments and programs should provide instructors with sample assignments" showing how ethical AI use "is addressed and disclosed" is institutional support for instructors designing AI-aware assignments; P63 fits best since it supports faculty, though P35 concerns the redesign itself.
units.anchor: Departments and programs should provide instructors with sample assignments

units.why: The page points instructors to "more information and training related to Generative AI at Marshall University", offering faculty training (P63).
units.anchor: for more information and training related to Generative AI at Marshall University.

documents.title: Responsible use of AI at Marshall University
documents.stance_why: The page says "Marshall University encourages students to use AI tools responsibly" and "encourages the appropriate use of AI", a welcoming stance with responsibility conditions, and no ban.
documents.summary: University responsible-use page encourages responsible student AI use and stresses integrity, verification, attribution and data protection. It also covers vetted tools, faculty resources and Microsoft Copilot data protection.

units.why: Faculty, staff and partners "should use only approved technologies when storing, processing, or sharing Institutional Data", a data-protection and vetted-tool rule (P50) that is not about students.
units.anchor: should use only approved technologies when storing, processing, or sharing Institutional Data.

units.why: "All technology solutions, including AI-powered tools and personal productivity applications, must follow the University's technology governance and review requirements" requires institutional review of AI tools (P65).
units.anchor: must follow the
units.frag_end: institutional information and ensure appropriate use.

units.why: The page says the Technology Governance Process reviews AI tools "for security, privacy, compliance, accessibility, and institutional risk before adoption", describing institutional vetting of AI tools (P65).
units.anchor: are reviewed for security, privacy, compliance, accessibility, and institutional risk before adoption.

units.why: "Faculty and staff should follow established review processes when considering new technologies" directs faculty to the review process before adopting AI tools; same type P65.
units.anchor: Faculty and staff should follow established review processes

units.why: "Artificial intelligence can support teaching, learning, research, student services, and administrative work" is a preamble stating the purpose of AI at Marshall, so P56 (framework/principles).
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence can support teaching, learning, research, student services, and administrative work
units.frag_end: use these technologies responsibly and effectively.

units.why: The text says understanding AI helps people "protect university data, validate AI-generated content", a general duty to validate AI output (P31); P50 is not chosen because the data aspect is coded in the student-specific unit.
units.anchor: validate AI-generated content

units.why: The CTL "provides a comprehensive set of resources aimed at helping faculty understand and integrate artificial intelligence" which is faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: helping faculty understand and integrate artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: Center for Teaching & Learning at Marshall

units.why: "Marshall University encourages students to use AI tools responsibly to support learning, research, and academic success" sets a welcoming default for students: P02.
units.anchor: encourages students to use AI tools responsibly to support learning, research, and academic success.
units.frag_start: Marshall University encourages students to use

units.why: The same passage lists "protecting personal and university data" as part of effective use, a data-protection duty for students (P50).
units.anchor: protecting personal and university data

units.why: "verifying AI-generated content for accuracy" is a duty to check AI output (P31).
units.anchor: verifying AI-generated content for accuracy

units.why: "being transparent about AI assistance when appropriate" asks for disclosure, but only where appropriate, so P24 with a soft modality (should).
units.anchor: being transparent about AI assistance when appropriate

units.why: "applying critical thinking and human judgment throughout the learning process" keeps the student as the thinker, which is P32.
units.anchor: applying critical thinking and human judgment throughout the learning process.

units.why: The page says the university encourages appropriate AI use "while maintaining academic integrity, proper attribution, and original scholarship", meaning submitted work stays original (P29); attribution is separately coded P24 in the previous unit.
units.anchor: maintaining academic integrity, proper attribution, and original scholarship.

units.why: "Microsoft 365 Copilot operates within Marshall University's secure Microsoft 365 environment" presents a university-provided, data-protected AI tool (P17).
units.anchor: Microsoft 365 Copilot operates within Marshall University
units.frag_end: institutional governance policies to help keep university data secure.

notes: No College of Engineering and Computer Sciences or CS department AI policy found; CECS news covers AI curriculum only.
